Maria L: Heads up — canary (~42%) is showing a 3x tail p99 regression for long-seq streams after the runtime merge (PR #6789). KV hit rate collapsed, eviction spikes. CI perf didn't catch it :grimacing:
Alex K: saw the observability alert. Which kernel variant did the selector pick? :eyes:
Maria L: kernel-autoselect now prefers 'kernel_v2' for seq_len >= 512. The change was meant to cut avg latency but looks like it causes KV cache thrash for our long traces. Profiler snapshots attached to the thread.
ci-bot: perf-profile job 6789 failed: p99 +120% vs baseline — https://ci.internal/perf/6789
Priya S: can we bisect to the offending commit? @Alex can you try reverting kernel selector change locally and smoke?
Alex K: starting a quick bisection now. Local repro on canary image repros the p99 spike. Reverting commit 0f3a4 makes p99 drop back to baseline in my smoke runs.
Samir R: will pause the A variant rollout while we confirm. /rollout pause canary-a
RevertBot: Rollout paused by Samir R at 2164006805
Maria L: quick mitigation proposal: add kv_hit_rate check into canary gating. If kv_hit_rate drops >30% relative to baseline or cache_evictions spike >x, autopause the rollout. Also add a synthetic long-seq test to the canary suite.
Priya S: here's the heuristic change that looks problematic (sketch):
```python
# kernel selector change (simplified)
if seq_len >= 512:
    prefer = 'kernel_v2'
elif avg_latency < 20:
    prefer = 'kernel_v2'
else:
    prefer = 'kernel_v1'
```
Alex K: the avg_latency branch is too permissive — sampling bias made v2 look better on smaller workloads and it got picked for long-seq requests, which thrashes the KV cache. I'll open a revert PR and add kv metrics to the selector decision.
Maria L: Revert PR submitted: #6792. Please run perf CI and add an autotest that includes kv_hit_rate and cache_evictions checks.
ci-bot: perf-profile rerun for PR 6792 complete: p99 -5% vs baseline, kv_hit_rate restored (+38%).
Samir R: /rollout resume canary-a -> Resumed by Samir R at 2164006875 :thumbsup:
Maria L: thanks all. Follow-up actions: (1) add kv_hit_rate & cache_evictions to canary SLOs, (2) require long-seq synthetic for kernel selector flips, (3) add a CI perf guard that fails PRs where p99 increases by >15% or kv_hit_rate drops by >20%. I'll draft a short playbook entry. :memo:
Alex K: added to my TODOs, will send follow-up PR to selector and tests.
Priya S: glad the rollback was quick. Let's also add a small note in the release checklist about runtime heuristics. :+1:
Maria L: filing postmortem and playbook link when ready. For now, tagging this thread into the canary incident doc. :eyes:
